FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Pesticides 
Sectional Committee had been approved by the Food and Agriculture Division Council. 


Carpropamid, technical is employed in the preparation of fungicidal formulations. Carpropamid is the accepted 
common name by the International Organization for Standardization (ISO) for 2,2- Dichloro-1 -ethyl-3methyl- 
cyclopropanecarbosylic acid-1-(4- chlorophenyl)-ethyl]-amide 


The empirical and structural formula and molecular mass of Carpropamid are given below: 


Empirical Formula Structural Formula Molecular Mass (g/mol) 
C¡sH¡gCl, NO 334.672

Cl 
Cl NH 
H,C 


In the preparation of this standard, due consideration has been given to the provisions of Insecticides Act, 1968 
and the Rules framed thereunder. However, this standard is subject to the restrictions imposed under the /nsecticides 
Act and Rules, wherever applicable. 


For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, 
observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 
“Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised)”. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off 
value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 


IS 16706 : 2018 


Indian Standard 
CARPROPAMID, TECHNICAL — SPECIFICATION 


1 SCOPE 


This standard prescribes the requirements and 
methods of sampling and test for Carpropamid, 
technical. 


2 REFERENCES 


The following standards contain provisions which, 
through reference in this text, constitute provisions of 
this standard. At the time of publication, the editions 
indicated were valid. All standards are subject to 
revision, and parties to agreements based on this 
standard are encouraged to investigate the possibility 
of applying the most recent editions of the standards 
indicated below. 


IS No. Title 
1070 : 1992 Reagent grade water — 
Specification (third revision) 
6940 : 1982 Method of test for pesticides and 


their formulations (first revision) 


8190 (Part 1): Requirements for packaging of 


1988 pesticides: Part 1 Solid pesticides 
(second revision) 
5682 : 1991 Open top drums and kegs — 
Specification (first revision) 
10946 : 1996 Methods of sampling for technical 


grade pesticides (first revision) 
3 REQUIREMENTS 
3.1 Description 


The material shall be in the form of whitish to yellowish 
powder, devoid of hard aggregates and free from 
extraneous impurities. 


3.2 The material shall also comply with the 
requirements given in Table 1. 


4 PACKING 


The material shall be packed in four layered cross 


bottom sack with innermost layer being of composite 
film PA/PE (0.02 mm/0.04 mm thickness). The rest will 
be three layers of 70 GSM paper with the outer most 
layer laminated with 20 GSM PE from inside. The 
general requirements given in IS 8190 (Part 1) shall be 
followed. 


5 MARKING 


5.1 The sack shall bear legibly and indelibly the 
following information in addition to any other 
information as is necessary under Insecticides Act, 1968 
and Rules framed thereunder: 


a) Name of the material; 

b) Name and address of the manufacturer; 

c) Batch number; 

d) Date of manufacture; 

e) Date of expiry; 

f) Net quantity; 

g) Nominal Carpropamid content, percent 
(m/m); 

h) Cautionary notice as worded in the 
Insecticides Act, 1968, and Rules framed 
thereunder; and 

j) Any other information required under the 


Legal Metrology (Packaged Commodities) 
Rules, 2011. 


5.2 BIS Certification Marking 


The product may also be marked with the Standard 
Mark. 


5.2.1 The use of the standard mark is governed by the 
provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 
and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The 
details of conditions under which the license for the 

use of the Standard Mark may be granted to 

manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the 

Bureau of Indian Standards.

6 SAMPLING 


Representative samples shall be drawn as prescribed 
in IS 10946. 


7 TESTS 


7.1 Tests shall be carried out by the methods referred 
in col 4 and 5 of Table 1. 


7.2 Quality of Reagents 


Unless specified otherwise, pure chemicals and reagent 
grade water (see IS 1070) shall be employed in the 
tests. 


NOTE — ‘Pure chemicals’ shall mean chemicals that do not 
contain impurities which affect the results of analysis. 


ANNEX A 
[Table 1, SI No. (i)] 
DETERMINATION OF CARPROPAMID CONTENT 


A-1 PRINCIPLE 


Carpropamid content is determined by High 
Performance Liquid Chromatography (HPLC) with 
UV-VIS detector using internal standard technique. 


A-2 APPARATUS 


A-2.1 High Performance Liquid chromatograph 
(HPLC) equipped with UV-VIS detector and coupled 
to a printer-plotter-cum-integrator. The operative 
conditions suggested below are typical, which can be 
changed provided the standardization is done. 


Column Stainless steel, Silica column, 
Sum, 0.25 m length, 4.6 mm ID 

Mobile Phase n-Heptane : 1,4-Dioxane (95 : 5 
v/v) 

Flow rate 2.0 ml/min 

Detector UV detector (220 nm) 

Injection volume 2011 


A-2.2 Microlitre Syringe — 5/20 ul 
A-2.3 Glasswares 


A-3 REAGENTS 
A-3.1 n-Heptane — HPLC grade or equivalent. 
A-3.2 1, 4-Dioxane — HPLC grade or equivalent. 


A-3.3 Internal Standard — Diethyl phthalate AR 
grade or equivalent. 


A-3.4 Carpropamid Reference Standard — of 
known purity. 


A-4 PROCEDURE 


A-4.1 Preparation of Mobile Phase 


Mix n-heptane and 1,4-dioxane in the proportion of 
95 : 5 (v/v) and pass through a membrane filter under 
vacuum. Homogenize the mixture using a magnetic 
stirrer and allow to attain the room temperature. 


A-4.2 Preparation of Internal Standard Solution 


Weigh out accurately 1.0 g of diethyl phthalate into a 
100 ml volumetric flask. Dissolve in a mixture of 
n-heptane and 1,4-dioxane (95 : 5 v/v) and make up 
the volume up to the mark with a mixture of n-heptane 
and 1,4-dioxane (95 : 5 v/v, see A-4.1). Shake well to 
homogenize. 


A-4.3 Preparation of Standard Solution 


Weigh out accurately 0.1 g of carpropamid reference 
standard of known purity into a 100 ml volumetric flask. 
Dissolve in 5 ml of 1,4-dioxane. Keep the flask for 10 
min with intermittent shaking. Add 5 ml of internal 
standard solution (see A-4.2). Make up the volume up 
to the mark with a mixture of n-heptane and 1,4-dioxane 
(95:5 v/v, see A-4.1). Shake well to homogenize. 


A-4.4 Preparation of Sample Solution 


Weigh out accurately a quantity of a sample equivalent 
to 0.1 g of carpropamid into a 100 ml volumetric flask. 
Dissolve in 5 ml of 1,4-dioxane. Keep the flask for 
10 min with intermittent shaking. Add 5 ml of internal 
standard solution (see A-4.2). Make up the volume up 
to the mark with a mixture of n-heptane and 1,4-dioxane 
(95:5 v/v, see A-4.1). Shake well to homogenize. 


A-4.5 Estimation 


A-4.5.1 Inject 20 ul of reference standard solution 
(see A-4.3) into the HPLC followed by the sample 
solution (see A-4.4). From the chromatograms of 
standard solution and sample solution measure the peak 
areas of internal standard and carpropamid peaks and 
compute the percentage of carpropamid as given in A-6. 

NOTE — Use guard column with packing material corasil type 

II normal phase (silica gel polar) or equivalent and change the 


guard column after 20 injections or when the peak shape gets 
disturbed. 


A-4.5.2 Retention Time (Guide Values) 


Internal standard (Diethyl phthalate) - 7.32 min 
Carpropamid - A - 12.40 min 
Carpropamid - B - 13.61 min 
Total run time - 20.00 min 
A-6 CALCULATION 

Carpropamid content, Mx Ax A, xP 


tb 
percent by mass MXARA 


IS 16706 : 2018 


mass of standard carpropamid in standard 
solution, in g; 

mass of the sample for test, in g; 

total ofareas under each carpropamid isomer 
peaks in the chromatogram of standard 
solution; 

total ofareas under each carpropamid isomer 
peaks in the chromatogram of sample; 
peak area of Internal standard in the 
chromatogram of standard solution; 

peak area of Internal standard in the 
chromatogram of sample solution; and 
percentage purity of carpropamid reference 
standard.

Review of Indian Standards 

Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of 


“BIS Catalogue’ and “Standards : Monthly Additions”.
